name: Ontario — private schools and home schooling
description: Ontario private schools are businesses or non-profits that file an annual Notice of Intention to Operate (Education Act s.16, due 1 September). The ministry provides no funding, regulation, licensing, accreditation or oversight of operations; it inspects only secondary schools seeking or holding authority to grant OSSD credits. Teachers need not be Ontario-certified. Home schooling rests on Education Act s.21(2)(a) ('satisfactory instruction at home or elsewhere'); PPM 131 asks parents to notify the board in writing each year; boards normally do not investigate; no funding.

attributes.legal_term: Private school (Education Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. E.2, s.16 — Notice of Intention to Operate)
attributes.registration: Annual NOI by 1 September; ministry publishes a list of all operating private schools (data.ontario.ca) with OSSD-credit status and association membership.
attributes.inspection: Only private high schools seeking or approved to grant OSSD credits are inspected; elementary and non-credit secondary schools are not, and need not follow the Ontario curriculum.
attributes.teacher_certification: Not required (Ontario College of Teachers certification optional).
attributes.diploma: OSSD only through an inspected credit-granting private school; ministry warns not all private schools can grant it.
attributes.consumer_warning: 'You must do your own research'; the lists are not endorsements.
attributes.homeschooling: Notify the board where the child last attended, in writing, before 1 September each year (PPM 131, 2002); board accepts it as evidence of satisfactory instruction and normally does not investigate unless reasonable grounds; no per-pupil funding; EQAO and curriculum documents available; ILC courses carry an administration fee; secondary-school entry assessed by PLAR.
attributes.online: Online private schools are private schools like any other: credit-granting online schools are inspected (e.g., Virtual High School, BSID 665681).
attributes.compulsory_age: PPM 131 (issued 2002) cites compulsory attendance from 6 to 16; the current statutory age range was not re-verified in Phase 1.
